e-3627.knowledge_point: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Natural Logarithm Function
e-3627.worked_solution:
The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{ \textrm{d} x}\left( \ln x \right)= \dfrac{1}{x}
$$

We apply our formula and get

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}   & = \left(5\ln x\right)'\  
                                                    & = 5 (\ln x)'\
                                                    &=5\cdot \dfrac{1}{x}\
                                                    &= \dfrac{5}{x}.
						  

}
$$

e-3628.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum Containing a Natural Logarithm Function
e-3628.worked_solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\eqalign{
			f'(x) &= \left(2\ln x+x^2-1\right)'\
			&=2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}+2x-0\
			&=\dfrac{2}{x}+2x.

}
$$

e-3629.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base
e-3629.worked_solution:
Here, we apply our formula for the derivative when the base of the logarithm is a number other than $e.$ By doing so, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
			\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}&=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(4\log_3 x\right)\
									 &=4\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\log_3 x\right)\
									 &=4\cdot\dfrac{1}{x \ln 3}\
									&=\dfrac{4}{x \ln 3}.

}
$$

e-3630.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent Line of a Logarithmic Function at a Point
e-3630.problem: Given that $y= \log_4 x + \ln x$,  find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
e-3630.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}
		&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( \log_4 x + \ln x \right)\
		&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\log_4 x) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\ln x )\
		&= \dfrac{1}{x\ln 4} + \dfrac{1}{x}.
}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{1}{xln⁡4}+\frac{1}{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{ln⁡4}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x) \\  & =2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =2e\cdot {1}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{1} \\  & =2e-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Given that $y=2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$
content.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x) \\  & =2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(2e{x}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =2e\cdot {1}^{e-1}-\frac{1}{1} \\  & =2e-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Given that $y=3ln⁡x+2{x}^{2}-5x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3ln⁡x+2{x}^{2}-5x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3ln⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{x}+4x-5 \\  & =\frac{3}{x}+4x-5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{3}{x}+4x-5)|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{1}+4\cdot 1-5 \\  & =3+4-5 \\  & =2\,.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find dydx at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have dydx=ddx(3ln⁡x+2x2−5x)=ddx(3ln⁡x)+ddx(2x2)−ddx(5x)=3ddx(ln⁡x)+ddx(2x2)−ddx(5x)=3⋅1x+4x−5=3x+4x−5.
